claims: 3DTAC-CDFT self-consistently determines rotational angles, defining chiral critical frequency omega_crit via the bifurcation of azimuth angle phi from zero to non-zero.
Critical frequency omega_crit decreases monotonically with neutron number due to (gd) and (sd) neutrons shifting angular momentum from short/long axes to the collective medium axis.
Boundary isotopes 120Cs and 134Cs maintain phi = 0 throughout experimentally accessible spins, establishing the natural isotopic boundaries of chirality in the Cs chain.

Configuration-fixed constrained CDFT proves 125,129,131Cs possess two distinct triaxial minima (gamma ~ 13-26 deg) supporting MchiD, while 127Cs is excluded from A1/A2 MchiD due to near-axial prolate shape (gamma = 0.8 deg).
119Cs demonstrates pure proton chirality based on pi g9/2^-1 (x) pi h11/2^2, and 126Cs demonstrates odd-odd MchiD based on the same 2-quasiparticle configuration.

boundary: 3DTAC-CDFT is a mean-field theory that does not yield discrete quantum energy splitting without collective Hamiltonian restoration
